title: eval-harness: integrate prompt-regression metrics into CI gating + hook
author: Marisol Chen
description:
Motivation: Prevent silent prompt-set regressions by surfacing eval-harness metrics in CI and failing when quality drops below configured thresholds. This PR adds a thin CI hook that runs a targeted eval job for changed prompt-sets and evaluates key metrics (accuracy, safety flags, BLEU-like similarity for prompt templates). If metrics regress beyond repo-configured tolerances, the hook fails the PR and prints a human-readable summary with links to the failing examples.

What changed: added a new eval-harness CI action (ci/eval/prompt-regression-check) that: (1) detects changed prompt-sets or model-serving stubs, (2) runs a reproducible eval subset (default 500 examples, configurable), (3) computes regression deltas against the baseline commit as well as rolling baseline metrics, (4) emits a machine-readable JSON report and a concise markdown summary for GitHub checks. The action integrates with the existing quality-gate thresholds in .evalrc and supports per-repo opt-in via .github/eval-config.yaml.

Implementation notes: the core of the hook is a wrapper script (tools/eval/ci_prompt_check.py) that calls the existing eval-harness runner with deterministic seeds and a capped concurrency to avoid noisy latencies in CI. Thresholds are configurable: absolute_drop_pct, p_value_threshold, and a suppression list for flaky prompts. We reuse the existing metrics plumbing in eval-harness (metrics/registry) and add two new metrics: prompt_regression_delta and prompt_regression_ci_flag. The CI action uploads artifacts to the run for post-mortem and includes a short list of counterexamples when failing.

Testing and rollout: local unit tests for the wrapper and integration smoke tests added to eval-harness CI. I ran the action against main with a controlled baseline and verified the check fails when we inject a synthetic degradation and passes when baseline is restored. Rollout plan: enable as opt-in for evaluation and docs repos first, then flip opt-in for redwood repo in two weeks after monitoring.

Related: ENG-2219 implements the wider gating strategy for eval metrics; QA-140 requested opt-in safety lists for CI. See discussion in Linear and the linked run artifacts.

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of baseline selection, threshold semantics, and potential flakiness mitigations. The change is intentionally isolated to CI and eval-harness integration; runtime serving paths are unaffected.

review_comments: Ethan Park (reviewer): Can we make the default sample_size for CI smaller (200) to reduce CI minutes? Reply: We keep 500 as default but make it configurable per-repo; added guidance in docs and lowered concurrency to 4 to save compute.

Nina Solanki (reviewer): How do we avoid flaky failures due to nondeterministic model outputs? Reply: We added deterministic seeds and a suppression list for known-flaky prompts; we also compute p-values and require both absolute_drop_pct and p_value_threshold to trigger failure.
Luca Moretti (reviewer): Please ensure artifacts are retained for at least 7 days for triage. Reply: CI action now uploads artifacts and workflow retention set to 14 days in the action config.
QA (comment): Can operations opt out for large repos where CI minutes matter? Reply: Opt-in config added (.github/eval-config.yaml) and repo admins can set enabled: false; rollout will be gated.
Marisol Chen (author): Addressed comments and pushed changes; updated docs, reduced noisy logging, and added more targeted tests.
additional_notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing production serving code; it only adds CI hooks and eval-harness integrations.
Ops: when enabling the action at scale, consider moving the sample execution to a dedicated runner with GPU access to match baseline model behavior.
Follow-ups: add a dashboard in Redwood Console that surfaces CI-gated eval failures across repos (ENG-2301).
release_notes: Add CI gating for prompt-set regression metrics: new GitHub Action 'prompt-regression-check' that runs eval-harness subsets and fails PRs when configured thresholds are exceeded. Opt-in via .github/eval-config.yaml. Includes docs and integration tests.
examples_of_failure_output: Summary: prompt_regression_delta exceeded threshold for metric 'answer_f1' (drop 6.7% > threshold 5%). See artifacts/run-430213/report.json for counterexamples.
Counterexample snippet: prompt_id=prompt_482: expected 'Yes, please.' but model returned 'I cannot help with that.'
Action: author can re-run with updated baseline or adjust threshold after triage.
